title: Motie van het lid Beckerman over een bevoegde instantie aanwijzen om ook deepfakeporno en andere onrechtmatige seksuele beelden offline te halen

reading.body:
Deepfake pornography of Dutch public figures was created and distributed on a platform with millions of monthly visitors. The synthetic sexual imagery featured entertainers, politicians, athletes, and members of the Royal Family without their consent. This is a case of a generative AI system deployed without controls to prevent nonconsensual intimate imagery, a known harms category. It would have taken content moderation, detection systems, or basic account verification to prevent the creation and distribution of such material.

The deployment failure enabled impersonation at scale. Women in public life discovered their likenesses used in explicit material they did not create or authorize. The platform's lack of safeguards allowed users to generate and publish the content freely. What is not established is who created the deepfakes, how they obtained the source imagery, or whether the platform was deliberately designed to enable this use or merely failed to prevent it.

The incident prompted legal complaints and calls for government action to shut down such platforms and designate authorities to remove nonconsensual synthetic sexual content. Multiple victims filed reports, citing existing revenge porn laws as a basis for criminal prosecution. This shows a gap between what AI systems can enable and what legal and technical infrastructure exists to contain the harms.

summary:
Multiple well-known Dutch women are considering legal action after discovering themselves in fake pornographic videos on an online platform that receives approximately 13 million monthly visitors. The manipulated content features the faces of Dutch entertainers, television presenters, Olympic athletes, current and former government officials, mayors, and members of the Royal Family. The outgoing Justice Minister called the videos disgusting and urged victims to file complaints with authorities.

Several victims have already filed reports or are exploring legal options. Deepfake pornography falls under revenge porn laws and is therefore criminal. According to legal experts quoted in the article, victims can file police complaints, potentially leading prosecutors to shut down the website, or they can pursue other options such as class action lawsuits, complaints to the data protection authority, or contacting hosting companies. A previous case involving television presenter Welmoed Sijtsma resulted in a 39-year-old man receiving a conditional sentence of 180 hours.
title_en: Motion by member Beckerman on designating a competent authority to also remove deepfake pornography and other unlawful sexual images offline
